heroHeadline: Day 388: Post-Sindoor Arms Race Accelerates — Pakistan Fatah-4 Cruise Missile (750km) Confirmed; Both Sides Plan ~14% Defense Budget Surge; IISS Warns India 'Gearing Up for Armed Conflict'
heroSubtitle: June 2, 2026: In the aftermath of the 23rd Shangri-La Dialogue (May 30–June 1), strategic analysts confirmed Pakistan's Fatah-4 ground-launched cruise missile (750km range, introduced May 2026 by the Army Rocket Force Command) is capable of striking Delhi and Mumbai — the latest escalation in a post-Sindoor arms race with no bilateral risk-reduction mechanisms in place. Pakistan Today's June 2 arms control analysis documented both governments planning ~14% further defense increases in 2026-27: India ($92.1B, 5th globally) and Pakistan ($11.9B, +11%), both driven by post-Sindoor rearmament surges. IISS Shangri-La assessment (May 29): India is 'gearing up for armed conflict with China and Pakistan' with fully militarized borders. Expert calls for nuclear risk-reduction centers, missile test notification agreements, and Track 2 nuclear dialogue remain unimplemented at Day 388. The ceasefire holds with no LOC violations since May 10, 2025. Bilateral freeze comprehensive: no ambassadors, $0 formal trade, IWT suspended with India's PCA 'null and void' rejection operative, Pakistan airspace ban through June 23-24, four back-channel contacts the only bilateral interaction.
footerNote: Data sourced from Indian MEA/MOD, Pakistan ISPR/MFA, UN Security Council, SIPRI, Crisis Group, HRW, Stimson Center
